quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Wine critics have traditionally assumed that blind taste tests reveal true preferences uninfluenced by price or label prestige, treating such tests as the gold standard for evaluating quality. A widely cited study found that the same wine, presented at two different price points to separate groups, was consistently rated as tasting better when participants believed it was more expensive, even though no blinding could remove the influence of expectation entirely once a price was mentioned. The finding has led some researchers to question whether any tasting evaluation can be fully separated from psychological expectation.
options: Blind Tests Confirmed to Fully Eliminate Price Bias
Price Expectations Shaping Perceived Wine Quality Even in Tests
Participants Who Rated Cheaper Wine as Tasting Better
Researchers Concluding Price Has No Effect on Taste
quests.correctAnswer: Price Expectations Shaping Perceived Wine Quality Even in Tests
quests.hint: Notice what blind taste tests are assumed to achieve and what the study actually revealed about the influence of price expectation.
quests.explanation: The assumption that blind testing fully removes bias gets challenged here, showing that price expectation still shaped perceived taste. The summary should reflect that persistent influence rather than confirm that blind tests eliminate it.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Cybersecurity firms have traditionally focused training resources on teaching employees to recognize suspicious emails containing obvious red flags like spelling errors or urgent threats. An analysis of successful phishing attacks at several companies found that the most effective attacks increasingly used polished, error-free messages that appeared to come from a trusted colleague discussing a routine, low-stakes task, precisely because they lacked the obvious warning signs employees had been trained to watch for. Several firms have since shifted training to emphasize verifying unexpected requests through a separate channel, regardless of how the message appears.
options: Polished, Low-Stakes Phishing Bypassing Traditional Warning-Sign Training
Obvious Red Flags Confirmed as the Main Attack Method
Firms That Stopped Updating Their Security Training
Employees Who Caught Every Polished Phishing Attempt
quests.correctAnswer: Polished, Low-Stakes Phishing Bypassing Traditional Warning-Sign Training
quests.hint: Consider what employees were originally trained to watch for and why the most successful attacks were able to avoid detection despite that training.
quests.explanation: Attackers adapted past the original training's focus on obvious red flags here, exposing a gap that required a new verification-based approach. The summary should capture that evolving threat and the resulting shift in strategy.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Public health campaigns promoting handwashing have traditionally relied on simple reminders about germs and illness prevention, assuming awareness alone would change behavior in most settings. A study placed at several public restrooms compared standard reminder signs with signs displaying real-time data showing the percentage of recent visitors who had washed properly, updated automatically by sensors. Restrooms with the real-time data signs saw meaningfully higher compliance than those with standard reminders, suggesting that social proof, knowing what others actually do, motivated behavior more than general health warnings alone.
options: Real-Time Peer Data Outperforming Standard Handwashing Reminders
Standard Health Reminders Confirmed as Most Effective
Social Proof Found to Have No Influence on Behavior
Compliance Rates That Were Identical Across Both Sign Types
quests.correctAnswer: Real-Time Peer Data Outperforming Standard Handwashing Reminders
quests.hint: Think about the two types of signs being compared and which one the study found actually changed people's handwashing behavior more.
quests.explanation: Two approaches are compared here, and information about others' actual behavior proves more persuasive than general awareness messaging. The summary should reflect that specific comparison and its result.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Video game developers have traditionally assumed that releasing a sequel as soon as possible after a successful original capitalizes on existing momentum and audience enthusiasm before it fades. A retrospective analysis of sales data across many franchises found that sequels released within one year of the original actually underperformed those released two to three years later, possibly because the shorter window left insufficient time to meaningfully improve mechanics, leading to player perception that the sequel was a rushed, minor update rather than a substantial new experience.
options: Sequels Released Within a Year Confirmed to Sell Best
Release Timing Found to Have No Effect on Sales
Players Who Preferred Minor, Rushed Updates
Rushed Sequels Underperforming Those Released Two to Three Years Later
quests.correctAnswer: Rushed Sequels Underperforming Those Released Two to Three Years Later
quests.hint: Look at the assumption developers made about quick sequels and what the sales data actually revealed about the ideal timing.
quests.explanation: The assumption that faster sequels perform better gets challenged here, showing that a longer development window actually produced stronger sales. The summary should capture that counterintuitive timing finding.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Corporate apology statements following public mistakes have traditionally relied on carefully hedged language designed to minimize legal liability, often avoiding direct acknowledgment of fault even while expressing regret. Communication researchers analyzing public reaction to dozens of corporate apologies found that statements including a direct, specific acknowledgment of what went wrong generated significantly more forgiveness from the public than vaguer statements, even when the direct statements technically created greater legal exposure for the company. Several companies have since revised their crisis communication policies to prioritize specificity over legal caution.
options: Vague, Hedged Apologies Confirmed to Generate More Forgiveness
Specific Apologies Earning More Public Forgiveness Than Vague Ones
Direct Apologies Found to Create No Legal Exposure
Companies That Removed Apologies from Their Crisis Policies Entirely
quests.correctAnswer: Specific Apologies Earning More Public Forgiveness Than Vague Ones
quests.hint: Ask yourself about the traditional approach to corporate apologies and what the research found about how the public actually responded to more direct statements.
quests.explanation: A strategy designed to minimize legal risk actually produces worse public relations outcomes here than more direct, specific language. The summary should capture that trade-off and its surprising result.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Productivity advice has traditionally encouraged people to tackle their most difficult task first thing in the morning, when willpower is assumed to be at its peak. A tracking study following office workers' self-reported energy and task difficulty over several weeks found that the timing of peak focus varied considerably between individuals, with a substantial portion of participants actually performing their most demanding cognitive work more effectively in the early afternoon. Researchers suggested that generic scheduling advice may be less useful than individuals identifying their own personal energy patterns through simple self-tracking.
options: Morning Hours Confirmed as Universally Peak Focus Time
All Participants Sharing the Same Peak Focus Period
Individual Energy Patterns Challenging Generic Morning-Task Advice
Researchers Recommending Against Any Form of Self-Tracking
quests.correctAnswer: Individual Energy Patterns Challenging Generic Morning-Task Advice
quests.hint: Identify the common productivity advice mentioned at the start and what the tracking study revealed about how much that advice actually applies to everyone.
quests.explanation: A generic piece of advice gets challenged here by showing that peak focus timing varies by individual. The summary should reflect that personalized finding rather than confirm the universal morning recommendation.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: University admissions offices have traditionally weighted standardized test scores heavily, assuming they provide an objective, comparable measure of academic readiness across applicants from different schools and backgrounds. A multi-year study tracking the college performance of students admitted under test-optional policies found that students who chose not to submit scores performed comparably in college GPA to those who did, regardless of the scores they would have submitted, suggesting that self-assessment of readiness was nearly as predictive as the test itself for many applicants.
options: Standardized Tests Confirmed as the Best Predictor of Success
Test-Optional Students Performing Significantly Worse in College
Self-Assessment Found to Be Entirely Unreliable
Test-Optional Students Performing Comparably Without Submitting Scores
quests.correctAnswer: Test-Optional Students Performing Comparably Without Submitting Scores
quests.hint: Focus on the assumption admissions offices made about test scores and what the study found about students who chose not to submit them.
quests.explanation: The assumption that test scores are essential for predicting success gets challenged here, showing that self-assessment alone was nearly as predictive. The summary should capture that comparable performance rather than confirm the importance of scores.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Performance review systems at many companies have traditionally relied on an annual rating scale, assuming a single yearly evaluation provides employees with sufficient direction for improvement throughout the year. Employee surveys at companies that switched to brief monthly check-ins instead of annual reviews found that employees reported feeling significantly more aware of how their work was perceived in real time, and managers noted catching performance issues months earlier than the annual cycle would have allowed, before small problems could compound into larger ones.
options: Annual Reviews Confirmed to Provide Sufficient Direction
Monthly Check-Ins Catching Performance Issues Earlier Than Annual Reviews
Monthly Check-Ins Found to Provide Less Useful Feedback
Managers Who Caught Issues Later Under the New System
quests.correctAnswer: Monthly Check-Ins Catching Performance Issues Earlier Than Annual Reviews
quests.hint: Picture the traditional annual review cycle and how the timing of feedback changed once companies switched to monthly check-ins.
quests.explanation: More frequent feedback allows problems to be caught earlier than the traditional annual cycle permitted here. The summary should reflect that timing advantage rather than confirm the sufficiency of annual reviews.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Travel guidebook publishers have traditionally assumed that comprehensive coverage, listing as many restaurants, hotels, and attractions as possible, provides the most value to readers planning a trip. A survey of guidebook users found that many readers felt overwhelmed by exhaustive lists and ultimately relied more heavily on a small number of strongly recommended, curated picks within each guidebook than on the complete listings. Several publishers have since restructured certain guidebook sections to highlight a handful of top recommendations more prominently, alongside the fuller, more exhaustive listings for readers who want them.
options: Readers Relying on Curated Picks Over Exhaustive Guidebook Listings
Comprehensive Listings Confirmed as the Most Valued Feature
Readers Who Ignored All Recommended Picks Entirely
Publishers Who Removed All Curated Recommendations
quests.correctAnswer: Readers Relying on Curated Picks Over Exhaustive Guidebook Listings
quests.hint: Compare what publishers assumed readers wanted from a guidebook with what the survey actually revealed about how readers used the information.
quests.explanation: The assumption that exhaustive listings are most valuable gets challenged here, showing that readers preferred a smaller set of curated recommendations. The summary should capture that preference rather than confirm the value of comprehensive coverage.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Adoption agencies have traditionally encouraged adoptive parents to introduce the topic of biological origins gradually, often waiting until a child asks directly before discussing details about their adoption story. Longitudinal research following adopted children into adulthood found that those who grew up with open, ongoing conversations about their adoption from an early age, rather than waiting for the child to initiate the topic, reported a stronger sense of identity and fewer feelings of having been deceived, even when the actual circumstances of their adoption were difficult to discuss.
options: Waiting for Children to Ask Confirmed as the Better Approach
Open Conversations Found to Increase Feelings of Deception
Early, Open Adoption Conversations Linked to Stronger Identity
Adopted Children Reporting No Difference Based on Communication Timing
quests.correctAnswer: Early, Open Adoption Conversations Linked to Stronger Identity
quests.hint: Weigh the traditional advice about when to discuss adoption against what the research found about children raised with earlier, ongoing conversations.
quests.explanation: Traditional advice about waiting for a child to ask gets challenged here, showing that earlier and ongoing openness was linked to better outcomes. The summary should reflect that research finding rather than confirm the wait-and-see approach.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Subscription box companies have traditionally assumed that offering customers the ability to fully customize every item in their box maximizes satisfaction by giving them exactly what they want each month. A customer retention analysis found that subscribers given a moderate number of curated choices, rather than complete customization of every item, actually renewed their subscriptions at higher rates, possibly because full customization removed the sense of pleasant surprise that subscribers reported enjoying about receiving a thoughtfully chosen selection.
options: Full Customization Confirmed to Maximize Subscriber Retention
Moderate Choice Outperforming Full Customization in Subscription Renewals
Subscribers Who Disliked Any Element of Surprise
A Company That Removed All Customization Options Entirely
quests.correctAnswer: Moderate Choice Outperforming Full Customization in Subscription Renewals
quests.hint: Notice the assumption companies made about giving customers full control and what the retention data actually showed about moderate versus complete customization.
quests.explanation: The assumption that maximum customization is always best gets challenged here, showing that some surprise and curation actually improved retention. The summary should capture that nuanced finding rather than confirm full customization as ideal.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Food safety regulators have traditionally focused inspection resources primarily on restaurant kitchens, assuming that is where most foodborne illness originates. An analysis of illness outbreak investigations across several years found that a substantial portion of traced outbreaks actually originated during food transportation and storage before ingredients ever reached a restaurant kitchen, often due to temperature control failures during delivery. Some regulatory agencies have since begun extending inspection requirements to cover transportation logistics, not just the final preparation site.
options: Restaurant Kitchens Confirmed as the Primary Source of Outbreaks
Transportation and Storage Found to Have No Role in Outbreaks
Agencies That Removed Kitchen Inspections Entirely
Outbreak Data Pointing to Transportation, Not Just Kitchens
quests.correctAnswer: Outbreak Data Pointing to Transportation, Not Just Kitchens
quests.hint: Consider where regulators traditionally focused their attention and what the outbreak data actually revealed about another important source of contamination.
quests.explanation: A significant source of foodborne illness was being overlooked here because inspection focus was too narrow. The summary should capture that broader finding about transportation, not just confirm the traditional kitchen-focused approach.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Ride-sharing companies have traditionally assumed that surge pricing during high-demand periods primarily serves to balance supply and demand by incentivizing more drivers to get on the road quickly. An analysis of driver behavior during surge periods found that a notable portion of drivers actually became less likely to accept rides during the highest surge multipliers, holding out in hopes that prices would climb even further before they committed to a trip, which sometimes left demand unmet even as prices spiked dramatically.
options: Surge Pricing Confirmed to Reliably Increase Driver Availability
Drivers Who Always Accepted Rides Regardless of Surge Level
Drivers Delaying Rides During Surges, Undermining the Pricing Goal
Demand That Was Always Fully Met During Surge Periods
quests.correctAnswer: Drivers Delaying Rides During Surges, Undermining the Pricing Goal
quests.hint: Think about what surge pricing is intended to achieve and what the analysis of actual driver behavior revealed about whether it always worked as intended.
quests.explanation: The pricing mechanism sometimes produces the opposite of its intended effect here, with drivers waiting rather than responding immediately. The summary should capture that unintended consequence rather than confirm the system worked as designed.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Mental health apps offering guided meditation have traditionally marketed longer daily sessions as providing greater benefit, assuming more meditation time straightforwardly produces more stress reduction. A study comparing users assigned to five-minute daily sessions with users assigned to twenty-minute sessions found comparable reductions in self-reported stress between the two groups after eight weeks, though the five-minute group showed substantially higher rates of continuing the practice consistently throughout the study period.
options: Short Sessions Matching Longer Ones in Benefit, Beating Them in Consistency
Twenty-Minute Sessions Confirmed to Produce Far Greater Benefit
Five-Minute Sessions Found to Provide No Stress Reduction
Both Groups Showing Identical Rates of Continued Practice
quests.correctAnswer: Short Sessions Matching Longer Ones in Benefit, Beating Them in Consistency
quests.hint: Look at the assumption that longer meditation sessions provide proportionally more benefit, and compare both the stress reduction and the consistency results between the two groups.
quests.explanation: Shorter sessions matched longer ones in benefit here while being easier to sustain consistently. The summary should capture both halves of that finding rather than focus on only the stress reduction or only the consistency.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Music streaming platforms have traditionally assumed that algorithmically generated playlists work best when optimized purely for predicted listener enjoyment of each individual song. A platform that experimented with intentionally including occasional songs from genres a listener had never explored, clearly labeled as exploratory picks, found that listeners who encountered these labeled surprises reported greater overall trust in the platform's recommendations, even when they skipped the exploratory songs themselves more often than their usual recommended tracks.
options: Pure Enjoyment Optimization Confirmed to Build the Most Trust
Listeners Who Never Skipped Any Exploratory Songs
Labeled Exploratory Songs Building Trust Despite Being Skipped Often
A Platform That Removed All Experimental Recommendations
quests.correctAnswer: Labeled Exploratory Songs Building Trust Despite Being Skipped Often
quests.hint: Ask yourself what the platform assumed mattered most for trust, and notice the contrast between how often songs were skipped and how listeners actually felt about the platform.
quests.explanation: Trust does not depend on listeners liking every song here, since skipped exploratory tracks still increase trust through transparency. The summary should capture that nuanced result rather than focus only on enjoyment optimization.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Public transit agencies have traditionally communicated service disruptions primarily through announcements at the affected station itself, assuming most riders learn about delays once they are already nearby. An agency that began sending push notifications to a transit app the moment a disruption was detected, rather than waiting for station announcements, found that riders receiving early notifications were significantly more likely to choose an alternate route in time, compared to riders who only learned about the disruption after already arriving at an affected station.
options: Station Announcements Confirmed as the Fastest Way to Inform Riders
Early Push Notifications Helping Riders Avoid Affected Stations
Riders Who Ignored Push Notifications Entirely
An Agency That Removed All Forms of Disruption Communication
quests.correctAnswer: Early Push Notifications Helping Riders Avoid Affected Stations
quests.hint: Identify when riders traditionally learned about disruptions and how receiving earlier notifications changed what they were able to do about it.
quests.explanation: Earlier communication gives riders more time to act here, leading to a meaningful behavior change compared to the traditional station-based announcements. The summary should capture that timing advantage.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Sleep researchers have traditionally advised against checking the time during nighttime awakenings, assuming the act of looking at a clock itself increases anxiety and makes returning to sleep harder. A study tracking participants who experienced insomnia found that those who covered their bedside clocks entirely fell back asleep only marginally faster than those who could see the time, suggesting that the anxiety often attributed to clock-watching may actually stem more from the underlying worry about insomnia itself than from the clock as a physical object.
options: Underlying Worry, Not the Clock Itself, Behind Most Sleep Anxiety
Covering the Clock Confirmed to Dramatically Improve Sleep
Participants Who Saw the Time Falling Asleep Far Faster
Researchers Concluding the Clock Has No Connection to Anxiety
quests.correctAnswer: Underlying Worry, Not the Clock Itself, Behind Most Sleep Anxiety
quests.hint: Focus on what sleep researchers traditionally blamed for nighttime anxiety and what the study suggests is actually the deeper cause.
quests.explanation: An assumption about the clock itself causing anxiety gets challenged here, suggesting the underlying worry about insomnia is the real driver. The summary should reflect that more nuanced explanation rather than confirm the clock as the primary cause.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: School librarians have traditionally organized reading collections primarily by genre, assuming students search for books mainly based on category preferences like mystery or fantasy. A survey of student borrowing patterns at one library found that a majority of students actually searched for books based on emotional tone, wanting something funny, sad, or comforting, regardless of genre, leading the library to add mood-based shelf labels alongside its traditional genre organization, after which overall circulation increased noticeably.
options: Genre Organization Confirmed as the Best Match for Student Searches
Students Found to Have No Preference Beyond Genre
Circulation That Declined After Adding Mood-Based Labels
Mood-Based Labels Boosting Circulation by Matching How Students Search
quests.correctAnswer: Mood-Based Labels Boosting Circulation by Matching How Students Search
quests.hint: Picture what the library originally assumed about how students search for books and what the survey actually revealed about their real searching habits.
quests.explanation: Students' actual searching habits did not match the library's genre-based assumption here, and adapting the organization to mood increased circulation. The summary should capture that discovery and its positive result.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Corporate training departments have traditionally measured the effectiveness of leadership development programs primarily through participant satisfaction surveys completed immediately after each session. A company that instead tracked participants' actual team performance metrics for a full year following training found little correlation between how highly participants rated a session and whether their teams showed measurable improvement afterward, with some lower-rated, less entertaining sessions correlating more strongly with long-term behavioral change than the most popular, well-reviewed ones.
options: Long-Term Performance Data Contradicting Immediate Satisfaction Ratings
Satisfaction Ratings Confirmed to Predict Long-Term Performance
Less Popular Sessions Found to Have No Lasting Effect
A Company That Stopped Tracking Any Training Outcomes
quests.correctAnswer: Long-Term Performance Data Contradicting Immediate Satisfaction Ratings
quests.hint: Compare what the company originally used to measure training success with what the year-long performance data revealed about whether that measurement was accurate.
quests.explanation: Immediate satisfaction does not reliably predict actual long-term improvement here. The summary should capture that mismatch rather than confirm that the most popular sessions were the most effective.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Theme parks have traditionally assumed that adding more thrilling, high-intensity rides each year is the most effective way to drive repeat visits from their most loyal customers. A loyalty program data analysis at one major park found that the strongest predictor of a family's likelihood to return within the same year was not the addition of new rides at all, but rather positive interactions with staff members during their previous visit, a factor the park had not previously tracked or actively measured.
options: New Thrill Rides Confirmed as the Strongest Predictor of Return Visits
Staff Interactions Predicting Return Visits More Than New Rides
Staff Interactions Found to Have No Effect on Loyalty
A Park That Stopped Tracking Loyalty Program Data Entirely
quests.correctAnswer: Staff Interactions Predicting Return Visits More Than New Rides
quests.hint: Weigh what the park traditionally assumed drove repeat visits against what the loyalty data actually identified as the strongest predictor instead.
quests.explanation: An assumption about new rides driving loyalty gets challenged here, identifying staff interaction as the overlooked stronger factor. The summary should reflect that surprising finding rather than confirm the value of adding new rides.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Co-parenting guidance following divorce has traditionally encouraged parents to maintain strictly separate households with minimal direct communication, assuming this reduces conflict exposure for children. A study comparing children across different co-parenting communication styles found that children whose parents maintained respectful, business-like communication directly with each other reported feeling less burdened than children whose parents avoided direct contact entirely, often relying on the children themselves to relay messages between households.
options: Minimal Communication Confirmed to Reduce Children's Burden Most
Children Who Relayed Messages Reporting Less Stress Overall
Direct Parent Communication Easing Children's Burden More Than Avoidance
A Study Finding No Connection Between Communication Style and Children
quests.correctAnswer: Direct Parent Communication Easing Children's Burden More Than Avoidance
quests.hint: Notice the traditional advice to avoid direct contact between parents and what the study found about children whose parents communicated directly instead.
quests.explanation: Traditional advice favoring minimal contact gets challenged here, showing that direct, respectful communication actually reduced children's burden more than relying on children as messengers. The summary should reflect that finding.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: E-commerce platforms have traditionally assumed that displaying the highest possible number of customer reviews next to a product builds the most trust and confidence in potential buyers. A study testing different review display formats found that shoppers presented with a smaller number of detailed, verified-purchase reviews trusted the product information more and converted to purchase at a higher rate than shoppers shown a much larger total review count without the same verification emphasis.
options: Larger Review Counts Confirmed to Build the Most Trust
Verified Reviews Found to Reduce Purchase Conversion
Shoppers Who Ignored Review Counts Entirely
Fewer Verified Reviews Building More Trust Than a Large Total Count
quests.correctAnswer: Fewer Verified Reviews Building More Trust Than a Large Total Count
quests.hint: Consider the assumption platforms made about review quantity and what the study found about quality and verification compared to sheer numbers.
quests.explanation: An assumption that more reviews automatically means more trust gets challenged here, showing that verification and detail mattered more than total count. The summary should reflect that quality-over-quantity finding.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Meal-kit delivery companies have traditionally assumed that providing the maximum amount of recipe variety each week, with no two weeks ever repeating a dish, keeps subscribers most engaged and prevents boredom with the service. A retention study found that subscribers actually canceled at a slightly higher rate when faced with constant total variety, citing decision fatigue from choosing among entirely unfamiliar recipes every single week, compared to subscribers offered a mix of new recipes alongside a few recurring favorites they could choose to repeat.
options: Maximum Variety Confirmed to Maximize Subscriber Retention
Subscribers Who Preferred Choosing Among Entirely Unfamiliar Recipes
Constant Recipe Variety Increasing Cancellations Through Decision Fatigue
A Company That Removed All Recipe Choices Entirely
quests.correctAnswer: Constant Recipe Variety Increasing Cancellations Through Decision Fatigue
quests.hint: Think about what the company assumed about variety and engagement, and what the retention study actually found about subscribers facing constant new choices.
quests.explanation: An assumption that maximum variety is always engaging gets overturned here, showing that some familiarity reduced decision fatigue and improved retention. The summary should capture that nuanced finding.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Software companies have traditionally assumed that releasing frequent, small feature updates keeps users engaged by continuously offering something new to discover. User research at one company found that frequent small updates instead left many users feeling disoriented, since familiar menus and buttons kept shifting locations before users had fully learned the previous layout, leading some long-time users to abandon the product in favor of a competitor with a more stable interface.
options: Frequent Updates Confirmed to Keep Users Consistently Engaged
Users Who Welcomed Constantly Shifting Menus and Layouts
A Competitor That Lost Users Due to Interface Stability
Frequent Small Updates Disorienting Users Rather Than Engaging Them
quests.correctAnswer: Frequent Small Updates Disorienting Users Rather Than Engaging Them
quests.hint: Look at what the company assumed frequent updates would achieve and what the user research actually revealed about the effect of constant interface changes.
quests.explanation: An assumption that frequent updates are inherently engaging gets challenged here, showing they instead caused disorientation and user loss. The summary should reflect that negative consequence rather than confirm the original assumption.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Hospital discharge planning has traditionally focused primarily on ensuring patients understand their medication instructions before leaving, assuming medication confusion is the leading cause of post-discharge complications. A review of readmission cases found that transportation difficulties getting to follow-up appointments were a more common underlying factor than medication misunderstanding in many readmitted patients, particularly among those without reliable access to a vehicle or nearby public transit. Some hospitals have since begun screening for transportation barriers as part of standard discharge planning.
options: Medication Confusion Confirmed as the Leading Cause of Readmission
Transportation Barriers Outweighing Medication Confusion in Readmissions
Transportation Barriers Found to Have No Effect on Readmission
Hospitals That Stopped Screening for Any Discharge Risk Factors
quests.correctAnswer: Transportation Barriers Outweighing Medication Confusion in Readmissions
quests.hint: Ask yourself what discharge planning traditionally focused on and what the readmission review actually identified as a more common underlying cause.
quests.explanation: The assumption that medication confusion is the primary driver of readmission gets challenged here, identifying transportation as an overlooked but more common factor. The summary should reflect that finding.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Comedy club bookers have traditionally assumed that headlining slots should go to the most experienced comedians with the longest set lengths, on the theory that audiences want to see established performers given the most stage time. An attendance analysis at one club found that shows featuring a rotating lineup of shorter sets from several comedians, rather than one long headliner set, generated noticeably higher repeat attendance, since audience members returned hoping to see how different comedians' shorter sets compared to one another.
options: Rotating Shorter Sets Driving More Repeat Attendance Than Long Headliners
Long Headliner Sets Confirmed to Maximize Repeat Attendance
Audiences Who Disliked Comparing Different Comedians
A Club That Removed All Headliner Slots Entirely
quests.correctAnswer: Rotating Shorter Sets Driving More Repeat Attendance Than Long Headliners
quests.hint: Identify the traditional booking assumption about experienced headliners and what the attendance data actually showed about a rotating shorter-set format.
quests.explanation: An assumption favoring long headliner sets gets challenged here, showing that variety across shorter sets drove more repeat visits. The summary should reflect that comparative finding rather than confirm the value of a single long headliner.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Utility companies have traditionally sent shutoff warning notices using formal legal language intended to clearly establish the company met its legal notification requirements before service interruption. A study analyzing customer response to these notices found that a significant portion of recipients did not realize the notice indicated an imminent shutoff at all, often mistaking the formal language for a routine billing statement, leading to recommendations that utilities add a simple, plain-language headline summarizing the urgent action required at the top of each notice.
options: Formal Notices Confirmed to Clearly Communicate Urgency
Customers Who Always Recognized the Shutoff Warning Immediately
Formal Legal Language Causing Customers to Miss Urgent Shutoff Notices
Utilities That Removed All Shutoff Notices Entirely
quests.correctAnswer: Formal Legal Language Causing Customers to Miss Urgent Shutoff Notices
quests.hint: Focus on why the utility companies originally used formal legal language and what the study revealed about how customers actually understood, or misunderstood, that language.
quests.explanation: Language designed to satisfy legal requirements fails to communicate urgency to many customers here. The summary should capture that comprehension gap rather than assume the formal notices worked as intended.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Time management experts have traditionally recommended batching similar small errands together into a single trip to maximize efficiency, assuming fewer total trips always saves more time and effort overall. A self-tracking experiment comparing batched errand days with spreading the same errands across the week found that while batching did reduce total travel time, participants reported significantly higher stress and exhaustion on batched days, leading several participants to conclude that spreading errands out, despite being technically less efficient, actually felt more sustainable for their overall wellbeing.
options: Batching Confirmed to Improve Both Efficiency and Wellbeing
Errand Batching Saving Time but Costing Wellbeing Compared to Spreading Tasks
Spreading Errands Found to Take Less Total Time
Participants Who Reported No Difference in Stress Between Approaches
quests.correctAnswer: Errand Batching Saving Time but Costing Wellbeing Compared to Spreading Tasks
quests.hint: Picture the two different outcomes the experiment measured, total time versus stress, and notice that the two approaches did not agree on which one was better.
quests.explanation: A trade-off between technical efficiency and personal wellbeing shows up here, with batching winning on time but losing on stress. The summary should capture that tension rather than declare one approach simply better overall.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Education researchers have traditionally assumed that smaller class sizes universally improve learning outcomes by allowing teachers to give each student more individual attention. A large-scale study comparing outcomes across various class sizes found that the benefit of smaller classes was strongly concentrated among younger students and largely disappeared by the upper grades, where student self-direction and instructional clarity seemed to matter more than class size itself for older students' academic performance.
options: Smaller Class Benefits Concentrated in Younger Grades, Fading Later
Smaller Classes Confirmed to Help Equally at Every Age
Class Size Found to Have No Effect at Any Age
Older Students Found to Benefit Most from Smaller Classes
quests.correctAnswer: Smaller Class Benefits Concentrated in Younger Grades, Fading Later
quests.hint: Compare the traditional assumption that smaller classes always help with how the actual benefit changed depending on students' age.
quests.explanation: A broad assumption about class size gets refined here by showing the benefit depends heavily on age, fading among older students. The summary should capture that nuanced, age-dependent finding rather than treat the benefit as universal.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Office productivity consultants have traditionally recommended minimizing all interruptions during the workday, treating any unplanned conversation as a costly distraction from focused work. A workplace study tracking actual project outcomes found that teams with a moderate amount of brief, informal interruptions, such as quick hallway questions, completed complex collaborative projects faster overall than teams that minimized interruptions entirely, since small clarifying conversations prevented larger misunderstandings from accumulating and requiring far more time to untangle later.
options: Minimizing All Interruptions Confirmed to Speed Up Projects
Teams with Frequent Interruptions Found to Complete Projects Slower
Researchers Concluding Interruptions Have No Effect on Project Speed
Brief Interruptions Speeding Up Collaborative Projects, Not Slowing Them
quests.correctAnswer: Brief Interruptions Speeding Up Collaborative Projects, Not Slowing Them
quests.hint: Weigh the traditional advice to minimize interruptions against what the study actually found about teams with a moderate amount of brief interruptions.
quests.explanation: The assumption that all interruptions hurt productivity gets challenged here, showing that some brief informal exchanges actually sped up complex projects by preventing bigger misunderstandings. The summary should reflect that counterintuitive finding.
